```{r}
library(data.table)
source('R/placebo_revision.R')
ctx <- revision_context(getwd())
specifications <- if(params$specification=='both')c('no_covariates','with_covariates') else params$specification
show_table <- function(name,specification=NULL) {
  path <- file.path(ctx$out,paste0('revision_',if(!is.null(specification))paste0(specification,'_') else '',name,'.csv'))
  if(!file.exists(path))return(htmltools::tags$p('This computation has not run: it is subject to the cumulative-year gap audit gate.'))
  z<-ctx$csv(path,'revision report input')
  if(name%in%c('performance','gain_vs_TWFE')&&'s'%in%names(z))z<-z[s%in%c(0,4)]
  if(name=='performance') {
    z[,entry:=sprintf('%.4f (%.4f)',estimate,mc_se)]
    counts<-z[,.(n_simulations=min(n_simulations)),by=.(sample,nc,dgp,model,s)]
    z<-merge(dcast(z,sample+nc+dgp+model+s~metric,value.var='entry'),counts,by=c('sample','nc','dgp','model','s'))
  }
  if(name=='gain_vs_TWFE') {
    z[,entry:=sprintf('%.2f%% (%.2f)',percent_difference,mc_se)]
    counts<-z[,.(n_simulations=min(n_simulations)),by=.(sample,nc,dgp,model,s)]
    z<-merge(dcast(z,sample+nc+dgp+model+s~metric,value.var='entry'),counts,by=c('sample','nc','dgp','model','s'))
  }
  if(name=='balanced_year4_check')z<-z[,.(cells=.N,max_absolute_difference=max(absolute_difference,na.rm=TRUE)),by=.(balanced,variable)]
  if(name=='phase0_reproduction')z<-z[,.(cells=.N,max_absolute_difference=max(absolute_difference,na.rm=TRUE)),by=.(sample,variable)]
  if(name=='S4_heldout_overlap_check')z<-z[,.(overlap_counties=sum(overlap_counties),flags_identical=all(flags_identical),
    max_retained_count_difference=max(abs(revision_retained-heldout_function_retained))),by=.(dgp,nc,model,half)]
  if(name=='S5_observed_aggregate_check')z<-z[,.(simulation_cells=.N,all_six_models=all(n_models==6),
    max_observed_aggregate_difference=max(observed_range)),by=.(sample,nc,dgp,s)]
  if(name=='balanced_counts_check')z<-z[,.(simulation_cells=.N,all_counts_constant=all(all_counts_constant)),by=.(sample,dgp,nc,model)]
  if(name=='output_index')z[,filename:=paste0('<a href="../placebo_revision/revision/',filename,'">',filename,'</a>')]
  htmltools::tags$details(htmltools::tags$summary(paste(name,if(!is.null(specification))specification else '',
    '—',nrow(z),'rows')),htmltools::tags$div(style='overflow:auto;max-height:650px;',
    htmltools::HTML(knitr::kable(z,format='html',digits=4,escape=name!='output_index'))))
}
```

## Checks before the new comparisons

The whole main-simulation sample includes both halves. Each specification uses
its own backdated diagnostics. The comparison below reports correlations and
mean absolute differences on the same county/simulation keys.

```{r}
show_table('diagnostic_specification_comparison')
```

The supplied manuscript contains numerical tables A1/A2 for the historical
no-covariate restriction. CRPS, coverage, and interval score agree at displayed
precision in all 72 rows. Bias, MAE, relative bias, relative MAE, and their
printed standard deviations also agree. RMSE differs in 42 rows because the manuscript's
spreadsheet route took square roots of rounded MSE. Numerical S1 and covariate
tables are absent from this PDF; those results appear as figures.

```{r}
show_table('manuscript_table_spotcheck')
show_table('manuscript_table_availability')
```

## Sample definitions

S1 is the full prepared placebo sample. The inputs already require predictions
from all six models: S2 (TWFE-eligible) is identical to S1 and is omitted.
S3 reproduces the historical pooled pre-RMSE restriction. S4 excludes each
model's own strict `|held-out z| > 2` flags and keeps missing diagnostics.
S5 is the intersection of all six S4 retained sets within S1.
S3–S5 describe retained counties; they do not change the fixed decision rule.
For S3, pre-RMSE is first pooled by its median across model rows within
scenario, simulation, and county; retention is strictly below the 90th
percentile across rows within scenario and subgroup, exactly as historically coded.

The primary comparisons preserve the legacy horizon-specific samples: a county
contributes at event year s if it is observed through s. A separately labelled
balanced sensitivity uses only county/simulations with all years 0–4 at
every horizon; it does not replace S1. The historical screening flags are
preserved rather than recalibrated for the balanced sample.

Before these computations, the gap audit checked that an observed horizon s
contains all s+1 years from 0 through s. Trailing truncation after s is not a
gap. Missing leading years and internal missing years are reported separately,
as are row-order and duplicate-year problems. If any cell's shortened-cumulative
share exceeds 0.1%, or ordering/duplicate problems are found, the computation
stops. **Observed gap shares are 0% in every cell of both specifications, with
no ordering or duplicate-year problems.** This conservative operational threshold implements the requested stop
for non-negligible gaps; full cell shares are reported for review.

```{r}
show_table('gap_gate')
show_table('gap_audit_all')
```

```{r}
htmltools::tagList(lapply(specifications,function(specification)htmltools::tagList(
  htmltools::tags$h3(specification),show_table('window_check',specification),
  show_table('county_population_check',specification),show_table('diagnostic_availability_and_flags',specification),
  show_table('retention',specification))))
```

## Performance and gain relative to TWFE

Performance uses the existing subgroup means of cumulative counts and
Poisson-noised predictive draws. Gains are percent differences relative to
TWFE, paired by simulation; negative differences in loss measures indicate
lower error. Monte Carlo SEs use the paired influence of the ratio, including
the square-root transformation for RMSE. Signed bias and correlation ratios
are descriptive and can be unstable near a zero TWFE denominator.
Table entries show estimates followed by Monte Carlo SEs in parentheses;
gain SEs are in percentage points. Relative RMSE uses the original
predicted-aggregate denominator, preserving the Section 3/S1 definition.

```{r}
htmltools::tagList(lapply(specifications,function(specification)htmltools::tagList(
  htmltools::tags$h3(specification),show_table('performance',specification),show_table('gain_vs_TWFE',specification))))
```

The B1/B3/B4/B5 rows are the separate balanced counterparts of S1/S3/S4/S5.
They use the same complete-year county/simulation set at every horizon and the
same frozen screening flags. They do not replace the primary S rows.
Because there are no gaps, primary and balanced rows at year 4 should coincide.

```{r}
htmltools::tagList(lapply(specifications,function(specification)show_table('balanced_year4_check',specification)))
```

## Selected paper figures

S1 full sample is primary. S3–S5 plots describe retained counties. Balanced
plots are labelled as sensitivity analyses; the index lists the additional
core-county and other-metric exports.

```{r}
htmltools::tagList(lapply(specifications,function(specification)htmltools::tagList(
  htmltools::tags$h3(specification),lapply(c('S1_full','S3_historical','S4_own_z2','S5_common_z2',
    'B1_balanced_full','B4_balanced_own_z2','B5_balanced_common_z2'),function(sample_label) {
      path<-file.path(ctx$out,'figures',paste0('revision_',specification,'_',sample_label,'_NonCore_RMSE.png'))
      if(file.exists(path))htmltools::tags$figure(htmltools::tags$figcaption(sample_label),

  }))))
```

## Upper tails

Percentile bins use each model's own finite county diagnostics within
scenario, simulation, and subgroup. Deciles use average ranks for ties.
The top 5% and top 1% overlap the highest decile. Missing held-out values are
omitted from these diagnostic bins, but retained by the S4/S5 screens.
RMSE averages county squared errors within simulation, then across simulations;
its Monte Carlo SE treats simulations as the independent units.
Empty bins are not assigned zero error. The tables report the number of
contributing simulations and mean county count; the most extreme bins can
have substantially fewer contributing simulations, especially after balancing.

```{r}
htmltools::tagList(lapply(specifications,function(specification)htmltools::tagList(
  htmltools::tags$h3(specification),show_table('upper_tail_pre_rmse',specification),show_table('upper_tail_heldout_abs_z',specification))))
```

## Poisson diagnostics

The pooled dispersion statistic divides the sum of squared Pearson residuals
by the count of finite pre-period county-years with positive fitted means.
Zero proportions use finite nonnegative means and report their own denominator.
Held-out calibration uses the saved two-sided predictive mid-p and reports
the available count and missing share. No fits are re-estimated.

```{r}
htmltools::tagList(lapply(specifications,function(specification)htmltools::tagList(
  htmltools::tags$h3(specification),show_table('poisson_diagnostics',specification),show_table('heldout_calibration',specification))))
```

## Case-study null benchmarks

The placebo truth is zero. The subgroup effect is the mean of cumulative
observed minus predictive counts across counties and posterior draws, as in
the case-study summary. County heterogeneity reuses the existing Figure 4
expression: the posterior mean of draw-wise county IQRs, rather than a median.
The table gives the 2.5%, 50%, and 97.5% quantiles across simulations for each
event year 0–4. These are descriptive null benchmarks.

```{r}
htmltools::tagList(lapply(specifications,function(specification)htmltools::tagList(
  htmltools::tags$h3(specification),show_table('null_benchmarks',specification))))
```

## Validation summaries

The numerical checks reproduce Phase 0 for S1/S3, match the shared held-out
screen's retained counts on overlapping county keys, establish identical
observed aggregates across models for S5, and verify constant balanced counts
at every horizon. S5 is also checked as a subset of every model's own retained
set. Physical half membership and the assignment hash are checked before
diagnostics are used. Both computation runs verified that the protected
legacy scripts, results, and decision file were unchanged.

```{r}
htmltools::tagList(lapply(specifications,function(specification)htmltools::tagList(
  htmltools::tags$h3(specification),show_table('phase0_reproduction',specification),
  show_table('S4_heldout_overlap_check',specification),show_table('S5_observed_aggregate_check',specification),
  show_table('balanced_counts_check',specification))))
```
